rendered: The review cites MBBTBC9 as an example of how strains isolated from different environments show tolerance to individual physicochemical stresses.[1][2] As stated: marine strain MBBTBC9 survives temperatures of[3]4–50 ◦C, 0.5–7% NaCl, pH 7–13, and heavy metals (up to 500 ppm)[4]. This illustrates the broad environmental adaptability of the species, which sustains growth across niches ranging from marine sediments to glacier soils.[5][6][7] For comparison, the Himalayan glacier strain cited alongside it is reported as follows:[8]Himalayan glacier strain MTCC 4822 grows at 4–45 ◦C and pH 3–14[9]. Beyond temperature, salinity, pH and heavy metals, no further tolerance limits are given for MBBTBC9; the species-level discussion of stress adaptation mentions osmotic pressure among the factors shaping growth and stress tolerance.[10]
